correctness.rationale: Every period is the exact order of a unimodular 2x2 matrix. A^2=(2+pq)A-I gives four exact base orders; derived factorizations of A^r-I have the asserted minimum ternary valuations. The odd-prime binomial lifting argument proves the exact exponent for every e, including saturation. Separate valuations and residue-product counts cover all parameter pairs. The embedded independent finite brute-force checker verified every pair at e=1,2,3,4; infinite quantifiers are certified by analytic arguments, not tests.

value.rationale: The identical 2014 primary study explicitly isolates modulus 3^e, e>1, as a missing natural classification. This result fully resolves that case with a simple valuation law, exact parameter multiplicities for all exponents, and the exact e-independent maximal-period proportion 4/27. It is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a routine instance of a prime-level result; its counts add information beyond matrix-order lifting and are directly relevant to finite-state cycle selection.
